title: Disjoint closed substacks give a quasi-coherent quotient algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and let $i_a:\mathcal Z_a\hookrightarrow\mathcal X$ for $a=1,2$ be closed substacks in the sense of [lem-sfb-invariant-closed-substack-descent]. Assume that $|\mathcal Z_1|\cap|\mathcal Z_2|=\varnothing$, with underlying spaces as in [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets]. On the big fppf site of $\mathcal X$, in the structure-sheaf and quasi-coherent-algebra conventions of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], define $\mathcal B_a$ on an object $x:T\to\mathcal X$ by $\mathcal B_a(x)=\Gamma(T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z_a,\mathcal O)$, with restrictions induced by pullback. Then $\mathcal B_1$, $\mathcal B_2$, and $\mathcal B_1\times\mathcal B_2$ are quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-algebras, and the canonical restriction map $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal B_1\times\mathcal B_2$ is a surjection of sheaves of algebras. Under the defining section convention, a global function on $\mathcal X$ maps to its restrictions on $\mathcal Z_1$ and $\mathcal Z_2$. No Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Agent-formulated consequence of Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent); stacks-properties.tex Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation); morphisms.tex Tag 01QQ (lemma-closed-immersion-bijection-ideals); algebra.tex Tag 00DT (lemma-chinese-remainder). The consequence is stated on arbitrary algebraic stacks, not only schemes.

proof.text: For every object $x:T\to\mathcal X$, put $Z_{a,T}=T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z_a$ and $j_{a,T}:Z_{a,T}\to T$. The closed-substack definition makes this a closed immersion of schemes. In particular it is affine, and on each affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_{a,U})$, with restriction map the quotient map. Since $\mathcal Z_a$ is a strictly full substack and an object of the 2-fibre product over $T''$ is a triple $(t,z,\phi:t^*x\xrightarrow{\sim}z)$, the functor $T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z_a$ is the subfunctor $\{t:T''\to T\mid t^*x\in\mathcal Z_a(T'')\}$ of $h_T$, represented by $Z_{a,T}$. For an arrow $\alpha:y\to x$ over $u:T'\to T$ one has $s^*y\simeq(us)^*x$ for every $s:T''\to T'$, so $Z_{a,T'}=u^{-1}(Z_{a,T})=Z_{a,T}\times_TT'$ as closed subschemes of $T'$, independently of the choice of $\alpha$ over $u$; for composable arrows these identifications are the transitivity isomorphisms of scheme fibre products, and for an open $U\subseteq T$ the pullback is $Z_{a,T}\cap U$. Set $M_{a,x}=(j_{a,T})_*\mathcal O_{Z_{a,T}}$, with its ordinary algebra structure. The affine-pushforward theorem makes its underlying module quasi-coherent and, for every arrow $y\to x$ over $u:T'\to T$, supplies the canonical algebra isomorphism $u^*M_{a,x}\simeq M_{a,y}$. Its composition clause gives the required cocycle, and the identity comparison is the identity. Thus these comparisons apply to arbitrary base maps, including nonflat ones.

source.place: Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion); affine pushforward and base change as stated in the cited node.

proof.text: Apply the cartesian-module realization criterion to $x\mapsto M_{a,x}$ and the comparisons in step 1. Its section formula is exactly $\Gamma(T,M_{a,x})=\Gamma(Z_{a,T},\mathcal O)=\mathcal B_a(x)$, with the prescribed pullback restrictions. Hence each $\mathcal B_a$ is an fppf sheaf and is quasi-coherent. Pointwise multiplication and the pullback map from $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ commute with restrictions, since the comparisons of step 1 are algebra isomorphisms. They therefore make it a quasi-coherent algebra in the stated convention.

source.place: Tag 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent), applied to the explicit cartesian modules of step 1.

proof.text: On each $T$ the module $M_{1,x}\oplus M_{2,x}$ is quasi-coherent by the binary-direct-sum node. Its underlying sheaf is also the pointwise binary product. Tensor pullback commutes with this binary sum: the maps induced by the two inclusions and projections are inverse, since $p_ai_b=\delta_{ab}$ and $i_1p_1+i_2p_2=1$, identities preserved by the additive tensor formula. The two comparisons of step 1 therefore give compatible pullback isomorphisms for this family. The realization criterion gives a quasi-coherent sheaf whose sections are $\Gamma(T,M_{1,x})\times\Gamma(T,M_{2,x})$. This is exactly $\mathcal B_1\times\mathcal B_2$, with componentwise algebra operations and diagonal structure map.

source.place: Tag 06WK; finite direct sums and the explicit tensor-pullback formula.

proof.text: Fix $x:T\to\mathcal X$ and a pair of sections of the target over $x$. The base-change image clause of the topology node says the two closed supports $C_a=|Z_{a,T}|\subseteq|T|$ are disjoint. Thus $T\setminus C_1$ and $T\setminus C_2$ cover $T$. Refine each by affine opens. On an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T\setminus C_1$, the first pullback closed subscheme is empty, so its ring of sections is the zero ring; the second is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_{2,U})$ by step 1. The given pair is therefore $(0,b)$, and any representative of $b$ in $A$ lifts it. On an affine in $T\setminus C_2$ the same argument lifts $(b,0)$. These affine open covers are fppf covers, so every target section lifts locally. This is exactly surjectivity in the stated sheaf convention; no lifting on all global sections is asserted.

source.place: Tag 00DT (lemma-chinese-remainder), elementary local form: on the two open complements one quotient factor is zero.

proof.text: A global function is a compatible family $(f_x)_x$ in the structure sheaf. By construction its image at $x:T\to\mathcal X$ is the pair of pullbacks of $f_x$ to $Z_{1,T}$ and $Z_{2,T}$. These families are precisely its restrictions to the two closed substacks, since their values on every scheme object are those pullbacks. This proves the final compatibility. All preceding constructions allow arbitrary ideals and arbitrary base schemes, so no Noetherian or finite-type assumption has entered.

source.place: Structure-sheaf section convention, evaluated on the two closed-substack base changes.
